task_reconstruction.official_task: 2023 MCM Problem C, as restated on physical pages 4 and 5.
required_outputs: a model forecasting the number of reported results on a future day, with a prediction interval
whether word attributes affect the percentage of scores played in Hard Mode, and how
a model forecasting the percentages of (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, X), applied to EERIE on March 1, 2023, with an evaluation
a model classifying word difficulty, applied to EERIE, with a measure of accuracy
other interesting features in the data, and a letter to the puzzle editor

contributions.summary: The summary names five tasks and delivers a number for four of them, with the letter to the editor counted as the fifth deliverable.
A gated recurrent unit forecasts the daily count of reported results, and its four update lines are numbered as one equation.
The seven attempt shares are compressed into one score by an equal-weight sum, so the attribute analysis has a single response.
A grid-searched random forest maps three word attributes onto the seven shares for one word.
A sigmoid-rescaled version of the same score becomes a difficulty rate, and K-Means++ cuts it into five levels.
Gaussian noise is added to two of the three inputs so the model's stability can be read off the figures.

dependency_graph.handoff: The repaired daily counts are the series the gated model is trained on.
The rescaled daily percentages are the seven numbers the score compresses.
The single score is the response both regressions are fitted against.
The single score is the quantity the two box plots compare across groups.
The two frequencies survive the correlation test and become inputs.
Letter repetition survives the comparison and becomes an input; part of speech does not.
The difficulty rate reuses the score's two-part shape and rescales it.
The trained forest is the model whose inputs are perturbed.

assumptions.summary: The seven shares for a word stand for the Hard Mode percentage, because the two agreed to within 1% on Wordle 207.
Every player is equally likely to post their result, which is asserted with no evidence at all.
No player knows the answer in advance and none cheats, which is the only assumption stated with two denials.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Five recording defects are repaired in one table: three misspelled words and one mis-keyed count, each with the index of the wrong entry.
Days whose shares miss 100% are rescaled so the sum is exactly one, with the cause, the remedy, and the target each carrying its own connector.
Only the words from January 7, 2022 to December 31, 2022 are used, and the training window is stated for the forest but not for the gated model.

models.summary: The paper lists five repairs in a table and then states one constraint: the attempt shares for a day are recomputed so they sum to exactly 100 percent. The sum is printed with the index running from 1 to X and the right-hand side written as a percentage, not a fraction.

Four update lines are printed and numbered once, as equation (1). The reset gate and the update gate are sigmoids of an input term plus a recurrent term. The candidate state is a tanh of an input term plus the reset gate times a recurrent term. The hidden state blends the candidate and the previous state by the update gate. The forecast error is a root mean square, equation (2), and the forecast itself is an interval around a point.

The score is a weighted sum of two parts. The first is the mean number of tries over the bins from 1 to 6. The second is the share that failed, the X bin. Both weights are fixed at one half and the method is named after the numbers.

Letter frequency is defined as a sum of five letter frequencies, equation (4). The summand is written as a single subscripted term whose subscript lists the letters, and the sum runs from 1 to 5. No regression line is written. The paper reports Pearson and Spearman coefficients and reads the empty corners of the scatter as confirmation.

Words are split once into repeated and not repeated, and once into four parts of speech. Each split is shown as a box plot and a density plot. No equation is given. The verdict rests on the median gap, the box length, and the outlier gap, and the verb changes with the verdict.

The mapping is written as equation (5): the triple of word frequency, letter frequency, and repetition is sent to the seven bins by an arrow labeled G-SRF. The repetition input is set to 1.5 or 1 and then said to be normalized back to 0 and 1. The fit is judged by the mean squared error and the mean absolute error, equations (6) and (7).

The difficulty rate, equation (8), has the same two parts as the score, each passed through a sigmoid before weighting. The distance to a cluster center is the Euclidean distance, equation (9), and the fit is the sum of squared distances, equation (10). The centers are seeded by the plus-plus rule rather than at random, and the words are cut into five levels.

Gaussian noise is added to the inputs. The density is written as equation (11), with the square on the deviation and the two in the denominator of the exponent. The repetition input is excluded before any result, because normalization would cancel the noise. The verdict is read off the figures.

verification.summary: Eighty percent of the daily series is used for training and the remaining twenty for the test, with the dates attached to the first share only.
The error is judged against a ten-percent cutoff attributed to statistics and never derived, and against a relative RMSE of 6.4957%.
The two box-plot splits are read from the median gap, the box length, and the outlier count, with the third table column left empty for repetition.
Thirty sampled words are hand-labelled and compared with the clusters; 28 of 30 agree, and the count is printed before the 93.33% rate.
Gaussian noise is added to two inputs and the verdict is read from the figures, with no perturbed value quoted anywhere.

results_trace.summary: The relative error rate is 2.1569% and the relative RMSE 6.4957%, and the interval is printed as 20367 plus or minus 2.01569%.
The word-frequency correlations are quoted as -0.3165 and -0.2956 against a table that prints -0.3256 for the second.
The predicted shares for EERIE lead to a tuple of (1,7,23,30,23,13,3) and restate the table as MSE 20.70641 and MAE 3.24388.
EERIE's difficulty rate is 0.35916 and it falls in the third of five levels, with the level boundaries never printed.
The hardest word is parer at 0.98, and the two features behind it are that no attribute relates to the Hard Mode share.

writing_logic.summary: the age painted first, the game arriving only after However, the work landing in a shorter sentence after Thus
the stricter rule framed as an addition with What's more, the data source hedged between the subject and the verb
the weights fixed in the sentence and the method named after them
the earlier approach dismissed with Unlike and three signals of one claim
a check narrated as three verbs in the order the work was done, the count before the rate
the quantity of methods offered as the reason to replace them

language_observations.summary: The summary opens on the digital age and pivots with However, and every one of the five following paragraphs is launched by an ordinal that replaces a heading.
The three sentences of the opening shrink in order, so the shortest sentence carries the work done.
The background retells the summary's first sentence with conveyed swapped for accustomed, and What's more frames the hardest rule as a bonus.
The restatement is announced as questions and printed as five imperatives, the last left open with see if so a negative result still satisfies it.
The cleaning opens with the agent removed by a fronted participle and a passive verb, and shrugs at completeness with among others.
The score is justified by calling seven numbers difficult and not conducive, and the count is used once as the obstacle and once as the thing removed.
The two box-plot verdicts are separated only by their verbs: we believe for the difference that was found, we conclude for the one that was denied.
The new model is opened by granting the old one's strength with While and then naming what that model loses.
The result and the verdict both arrive before the definition, and scientific is attached to the method before it is described.
The sensitivity verdict is pointed at a figure and inferred with indicating, then repeated under the next heading with relatively inserted before low.
The strengths are labelled by algorithm with a colon three times and the fourth runs the label into its sentence with no colon and no space.
The letter keeps the summary's five ordinals, drops the hedges, and signs with the team number that appears in the page header.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A summary that reports a number for four of five tasks and hands the fifth to a letter reads as complete rather than selective.
Calling a point estimate plus or minus 2.01569% an interval, when the error rate two sentences earlier is 2.1569%, is the arithmetic a judge can check in one line.
Both error measures are declared very good under one adjective while sitting on different scales, so the claim cannot be reproduced from the printed numbers.

weaknesses.summary: Figure 3 is the GRU algorithm flowchart. The deviation plot is Figure 4, on the same page. A skill that copies the citation will describe a flowchart as a deviation curve. The skill may read a deviation series. It must cite the plot figure, not the flow figure.

The 10% rule is attributed to the discipline of statistics and never derived or cited. The paper's own error is 6.4957%, comfortably under it. The skill may quote a conventional small-error threshold. It must attribute it as conventional and must not present it as computed here.

The error interval is taken from the relative error rate 2.1569%, and the printed interval is plus or minus 2.01569%, a different number: an extra 0 arrives in the display. Only one of the two can be the interval the authors intended. The skill may report a point forecast with a percentage band. It must print one number consistently and must not reconcile the two silently.

The index of the sum is i but the summand is written in t, so the index never appears inside the sum. The formula as printed adds one term n times. The skill may write a root-mean-square error. It must use a consistent index and must not copy the printed summand verbatim.

The gloss puts X inside the index set while equation (3) sums i only from 1 to 6 and carries p_X as a separate term. If i can be X, the product i times p_i is undefined for the last element. The paper resolves the conflict in prose by saying X has no specific number of tries. The skill may keep the failure bin out of the try average. It must not sum the failure bin as though it had a try count.

The weights are declared to come from entropy weighting and are then fixed at one half and one half, which is the equal-weight answer that entropy weighting returns only under a specific symmetric input. No entropy calculation appears, and the same sentence appears again in section 7 for the difficulty rate. The skill may use equal weights. It must say they were set, not that they were computed by entropy weighting.

The summand is written once with a subscript that lists letters, so the value does not change with the index and the sum adds the same number five times. The intended reading is a sum over the five letters of the word. The skill may add the five letter frequencies. It must index the summand by the letter and must not copy the printed form.

The regression table is Table 5; Table 3 is the GRU symbol glossary on page 8. The letter-frequency paragraph repeats the same wrong pointer. The skill may point a reader at a coefficient table. It must cite Table 5 and must not inherit Table3 from the source.

Table 5 prints the word-frequency Spearman coefficient as -0.3256 and the prose prints -0.2956; the neighbouring Pearson cell matches exactly, so one cell is wrong and it is not a shifted row. The letter-frequency pair, -0.4238 and -0.4005, agree between prose and table. The skill may quote a rank correlation. It must not present the prose figure and the table figure as the same number.

The score is plotted on a logarithmic scale and no sentence in the paper says the score was transformed. A linear reading of the plot and a linear reading of the coefficients cannot both be right. The skill may plot a frequency against a compressed response. It must name the transform if it uses one.

No test is named, no statistic is printed, and the significant difference is read off a density plot. Table 6 leaves its third column, the outlier count difference, empty. The skill may compare two groups by median and spread. It must not call a difference significant without a test.

The repetition comparison is affirmed with we believe and hedged with a certain difference; the part-of-speech comparison is denied flatly. Both rest on the same kind of median comparison from the same figures, and the three part-of-speech median gaps are listed in full before the denial. The verdict verbs differ and the prose never says why. The skill may report both comparisons. It must not encode confidence in the choice of verb.

The three differences are numbered and never labelled, so which pair of parts of speech each compares cannot be recovered from the table. Two of the three values differ only in the fourth decimal place, so two of the three comparisons are effectively the same number. The skill may tabulate pairwise differences. It must label each pair.

A deliberate gap of 1.5 against 1 is chosen, and the next sentence says normalization will turn the same two values into 0 and 1, which discards the gap. Two sentences later the encoding no longer carries the weight it was given. The value itself is also copied as ref in the table header. The skill may encode a binary attribute. It must not record a magnitude and then normalize it away.

One frequency is printed with a percent sign and the other without, so the two inputs of the same model are on scales that differ by two orders of magnitude as printed. The skill may feed two frequency measures to a regressor. It must state the scale of each and must not mix a percentage with a bare ratio in one row.

The third header prints ref where the column holds rep under the encoding two paragraphs above. The table cannot be read as a list of the model's three named inputs. The skill may tabulate model inputs. It must print the input's own name.

Both error measures compare the prediction with origin data, and no origin data can exist for a future date. The numbers therefore belong to the fitted model on the training year and are moved onto the forecast day. The skill may report a training error. It must not present a training error as the error of a future prediction.

A squared-error measure of 20.71 and an absolute-error measure of 3.24 are judged by one phrase, very good, and no scale is given for either, so neither number is interpretable from the paper. The skill may report two error measures. It must give each its own scale or its own verdict.

The seven predicted shares sum to 100.01197%, not 100%, although section 1.3 promises that each day's proportions are recomputed to sum to exactly 100%. A predicted distribution that is off by a hundredth of a percent is small but the paper's own constraint is stricter than the model's output. The skill may report a predicted share vector. It must state whether it normalizes and must not claim a sum the numbers do not reach.

The sigmoid is written outside each weight and outside each sum, so the printed form rescales after weighting while the sentence before it says the two data are normalized and then weighted, which is the other order. The notation table also spends the symbol sigma on the difficulty rate while this equation uses sigma as the sigmoid function. The skill may normalize two parts before combining them. It must fix one order and one symbol.

The paper's own notation table names a symbol for the difficulty rate that the body never uses, and the body's symbol appears in no table. The table's glosses are also printed one row low, so the row for d carries the Euclidean-distance gloss among the error measures. The skill may keep a symbol table. It must make the table and the body agree.

The five levels are named and their boundaries are never printed, so a new word cannot be placed. Table 11 gives counts per level and the appendix gives each word's value and group, from which the boundaries could be inferred, but no sentence does it. The skill may assign a difficulty level. It must state the boundary rule or say it was inferred.

The columns Percentage and Valuable Percentage are identical cell for cell, so one of the two names has no content behind it. The table also prints five columns under four named headers. The skill may report a level histogram with shares. It must not print two columns of the same numbers under two names.

The three cells of the sum row are the bin-2, bin-3, and bin-4 values of Table 10 from page 16, carried into a table about cluster levels. Nothing in Table 11 sums to those three numbers. The level counts, 131, 152, 69, 7, and 1, sum to 360, and the level shares sum to 100. The skill may total a table. It must total that table's own column.

Section 8's two negative findings are stated with no coefficient, no p-value, and no number of any kind, while section 5's two positive findings are stated with four coefficients. The first assumption of the paper, that the seven bins can stand for the Hard Mode share because the two sets differ by only 1%, is contradicted in spirit by this section and no sentence connects them. The skill may report a negative result. It must give it the same evidence standard as a positive one.

The word is called second-place and the ranking is never stated as the paper's own, so an ordinal arrives as though the data supplied it. The value 0.98 is the appendix's 0.978421619 rounded, and the 0.69 is 0.685643564 rounded, so both headline numbers are roundings of a table the body does not cite. The skill may rank words by a difficulty score. It must say it ranked them and must cite the table.

A causal account of the hardest word rests on two unnamed social-media posts, and the two features it names, similar letter composition and similar positions, are not among the four attributes the paper measured. The skill may record a plausible mechanism. It must mark it as unverified and must not promote it into the model.

The excluded input is excluded because the model's own normalization would erase the perturbation, which is the same normalization that was said on page 15 to reduce the repetition encoding to 0 and 1. The exclusion is therefore an admission that the encoding carries no magnitude, and no sentence draws that consequence. The skill may drop an input from a sweep. It must give the reason as a property of the encoding, not as a property of the model.

The noise is defined by an equation with a mean and a standard deviation, and neither value is ever given, nor a seed, nor a number of draws. The perturbation is counted in units of noises. The skill may perturb an input. It must state the spread and the number of draws.

The verdict is read off two figures with no quoted quantity, and the letter-frequency verdict is the same sentence with relatively inserted before low. The summary then promotes both to low sensitivity and highly stable, dropping the hedge and adding an intensifier. The skill may report a sweep verdict. It must quote a quantity or mark the verdict as visual.

The advantage claimed is variable-length inputs, and the paper's own series is one value per day across a fixed window, so the strength describes the algorithm in general and not this use of it. The same strength sentence ends on the paper's own number by Therefore. The skill may name an algorithm's strengths. It must separate the general property from the property this run used.

The percent sign is dropped from the number the whole forecasting section rests on, so the strength reads as a bare magnitude. The same number appears with its sign on page 9, in Table 4, and in the letter. The skill may quote a relative error. It must keep the unit attached to the number.

The first three strengths are labelled by algorithm with a colon; the fourth repeats K-Means++ and then runs the sentence on with no colon, so the label and the content are glued. Its adjective, constructive, praises the analysis for being useful rather than correct, which is the only such standard in a section that otherwise judges accuracy and efficiency. The skill may list strengths by method. It must keep one label format and one standard of judgment.

Every misspelling in this paper is born in a table header, a figure caption, an axis label, or a heading, and each is then copied forward unchanged into the condensed versions. The prose is proofread and the labels are not. The skill may reuse a label from a paper. It must not copy a header or a caption as prose, and must not propagate a label defect into its own text.
